reason: Final dependency and axiom-contract audit: Let I_H(L) be the inertia group. If I_H(L)=N, the N-restriction is the direct sum of p pairwise nonisomorphic conjugates; the local-endomorphism exchange argument forces every H-endomorphism idempotent to be 0 or 1. If I_H(L)=H, reduce End_ON(L) modulo its radical to k (the residue field is algebraically closed). Mackey identifies the semisimple quotient of End_ON(Ind L) with M_p(k), while H-equivariance is the fixed ring under cyclic conjugation permuting the p diagonal idempotents. The conjugating matrix is one p-cycle and in characteristic p has a single Jordan block, so its centralizer is k[T]/((T-lambda)^p), a local algebra. The H-endomorphism ring is therefore local, and Krull-Schmidt makes Ind_N^H L indecomposable. These are the only inertia cases because the index is prime. Evidence inspected: Jin, Basic Modular Representation Theory, Theorem 4.1 and proof, pp. 6–7; Craven, The Brauer Correspondence, Theorem 2.20 proof, pp. 28–29.
